e.note: Best: A3 at 10.8% reach vs 4.0% for the benchmark

e.text: A3 leads at 10.8%, A2 close; asking the Critic how to combine podcasts, Stüssy and citywide ads.

e.note: Reading results for A1, A2, A3

critique.summary: A3 leads on mean reach (10.8%), 10th percentile (9.2%) and cost ($1366 per point), roughly 2.7x the benchmark's 4.0% at $2577 per point; A2 is close behind (10.3%, $1397), and its two podcasts alone account for 31.7% of adoption. What is not working: launch-week street teams and the $2500 pop-ups are credited with only 0.6–2.1% each, and A1 concentrates on two small zones (7.8% of the natural audience) for just 8.4% reach at $1609 per point.

findings.finding: The Stüssy drop carries 21.8% of adoption for $2000, but everything else is weak: the World Wide Tacos pop-up gets 2.1% for $2500, street teams on days 25–26 get 0.8% each, and reach of 8.4% (p10 7.2%) is the lowest of the three plans.

Bodega Boys (16.7%) and Drink Champs (15.0%) lift every district to 6.0% or higher, giving 10.3% reach at $1397 per point; Koreatown Galleria (0.3%) and the day-24 and day-26 street teams (1.0–1.4%) are dead weight.

Citywide targeted social earns 23.5% for $5040, against 28.9% for the benchmark's broad ads at the same price, and the early Fear of God drop adds 6.1%, yet Fear of God's 6.1% trails Stüssy's 21.8% in A1 at the same $2000.

The Exposition Park partners Wallis Annenberg and the California African American Museum, along with the day-26 West Adams street team, are credited with only 0.6% each, and the Exposition Park museum also scored lowest in A1 (0.8%).

changes.change: In A3, replace the Fear of God collab with the Stüssy collab (collab:92384FD1) and start it on day 0 for all 28 days.
changes.why: At the same $2000, Stüssy was credited with 21.8% of adoption in A1 versus 6.1% for Fear of God, and starting on day 0 gives word of mouth the longest runway.

changes.change: Add the Bodega Boys podcast around day 10 to A3, paid for by cutting the three day-26 street teams ($1350), the Wallis Annenberg and California African American Museum partners ($600), and social:3.
changes.why: Bodega Boys alone drove 16.7% of adoption in A2, while each of the cut items was credited with 0.6% or less.

changes.change: Drop the Wi Jammin pop-up on day 25 ($2500), or move it to around day 18.
changes.why: Launch-week pop-ups were credited with only 1.6–2.1% each across all plans, and a day-25 date leaves almost no time for word of mouth.

changes.change: Keep the Mid-City (zone 0) and Harvard Heights (zone 1) partners but drop Koreatown Galleria.
changes.why: Mid-City and Harvard Heights hold the largest shares of the natural audience (5.7% and 4.6%), while Koreatown Galleria was credited with only 0.3% for $300.

e.note: A3 leads on mean reach (10.8%), 10th percentile (9.2%) and cost ($1366 per point), roughly 2.7x the benchmark's 4.0% at $2577 per point; A2 is close behind (10.3%, $1397), and its two podcasts alone account for 31.7% of adoption. What is not working: launch-week street teams and the $2500 pop-ups are credited with only 0.6–2.1% each, and A1 concentrates on two small zones (7.8% of the natural audience) for just 8.4% reach at $1609 per point.

e.text: Applying the Critic's notes: Stüssy from day 0, Bodega Boys added, weak street teams and museums cut.

e.note: Revising: Base on A3: swap Fear of God for Stüssy from day 0, add Bodega Boys ~day 10, cut day-26 street teams and Exposition Park partners. Revision 1: drop the Wi Jammin pop-up and add Drink Champs. Revision 2: move pop-up to day 18.

plan.headline: Podcasts, Stüssy and citywide social reach 17.5% of the natural audience, 4.4x benchmark
plan.summary: The bet is to reach the crowd early through media they already over-index on: Drink Champs on day 5, Bodega Boys on day 10, a Stüssy co-branded drop from day 0 and 20 days of citywide social, so word of mouth has the longest runway. Qloo taste data shows this audience has very high affinity for Bodega Boys (0.98), Stüssy (0.96) and Drink Champs (0.95), and eight Mid-City, Harvard Heights, Leimert Park and West Adams spots score 0.80–0.87, pulled in by Kendrick Lamar, SZA and ScHoolboy Q. In the simulation this reaches 17.5% of the natural audience (range 15.9%–19.1%) at $852 per point, against 4.0% at $2,577 per point for the same budget spent where people are; that is a projection from a simulation built on Qloo taste data, not a guarantee.

weeks.label: Week 1 (days 0–6)
items: Day 0: launch the Stüssy co-branded drop. It runs the full 28 days.
Day 0: place all eight partner spots for the whole campaign: Wi Jammin, Leo's Tacos, START LA, Alibi Coffee, Southern Girl Desserts, World Wide Tacos, Vees Cafe and Mel's Fish Shack.
Day 1: start targeted citywide social ads (20 days, weighted toward best-fit cells).
Day 5: Drink Champs host-read ad airs.

weeks.label: Week 2 (days 7–13)
items: Day 10: Bodega Boys host-read ad airs.
Keep social running and echo the podcast reads in creative.
Check in with partner staff so they keep talking up the show, as at Southern Girl.

weeks.label: Week 3 (days 14–20)
items: Let word of mouth carry, since the simulation credits about half of adoption to it.
Restock flyers and Stüssy drop placements at partner spots.

weeks.label: Week 4 (days 21–28)
items: Social has ended, so partners and the Stüssy drop carry the final push.
Day 28: release show at the Wiltern.

risks: These projections come from a simulation built on Qloo taste data, not a guarantee; the range is 15.9%–19.1%.
Reach is weak in the podcast/sitcom district (9.8%) and the pop/Lululemon district (10.9%), and R&B-leaning listeners like Lauren may never see it.
South LA fans may hesitate to travel to Koreatown on a weeknight.
Half of adoption depends on word of mouth, so the result is fragile if early buzz is slow.
measure: Ticket sales by referral source (promo code per podcast, the Stüssy drop and each partner)
Social ad engagement and click-through by district
Mentions and shares tied to the podcast reads and the Stüssy drop
